title: Launch Thresholds & Bottleneck Decomposition — Sprint Playbook
body:
Purpose:
Short checklist + decomposition steps to convert high-level launch KPIs into actionable capacity and rollout gates. Meant to sit alongside the product launch playbook (ref above) but focused on explicit threshold math, early bottleneck detection heuristics, and quick mitigation recipes. Draft status — expect edits from SRE and Serving Runtime owners.

TL;DR (for exec skim):
- Required gating KPIs for soft launch (0-5%): p95 latency <= 450ms, error rate <= 0.3%, sustained CPU/GPU utilization headroom >= 20% for canary cluster, cost delta within expected budget +/-10%.
- If any two of (p95 latency, error rate, high KV-cache miss rate) breach, pause rollout and scale to dedicated pool or route to fallback model variant.

1) Key thresholds (explicit):
- Latency (generation requests, n=8k sample): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 450ms, p99 <= 900ms.
- Error rate (HTTP 5xx + model runtime errors): < 0.3% sustained over 5m, < 1% spike allowed for 1m if autobalancing occurs.
- Throughput: baseline 250 requests/s per 8x A100-equivalent pool for short context (<= 128 tokens).
- Token cost (hosted plan estimate): $0.16 per 1k tokens (avg); Dedicated target CP1: $0.05–0.08 per 1k tokens depending on quantization.
- Cache hit ratio (prefix KV cache): target >= 65% for repetitive traffic; early-warning if < 40%.
- Headroom: CPU/GPU utilization measured at pod level: keep target utilization in canary 55%–70% (above this, batch sizes risk growing latency tail).

2) Bottleneck decomposition steps (run during preflight):
A. Verify workload shape (sample traces + synthetic replay): median tokens/request, seq-length distribution, burstiness (req/s 1min/10s).
B. Map resource consumption to request types: embedding vs generation vs chat. Quick spreadsheet rows: [request_type, avg_tokens, avg_inference_time, avg_gpu_mem, batch_efficiency].
C. Simulate three stress modes: steady-state ramp (0->target qps over 30m), microburst (10x for 60s), long-tail (sustained at 1.5x for 2h). Record p50/p95/p99 and queue depth.
D. Observe KV cache behavior: instrument miss latency; if miss contributes >20% of p95, mark caching optimization action.

3) Canary gating checklist (0->5% traffic):
- Pre-canary: smoke test harness against staging model version, verify token-level counters, and run synthetic replay of 1k sampled requests.
- Canary launch: route 0.5% then 2% then 5% (step window >= 15m steady-state), watch rolling metrics.
- Gates (must hold for 15m at each step):
  * p95 latency not increasing > 15% relative to baseline
  * errors not spiking above threshold
  * KV-cache hit ratio stable or improving
  * operator confirmation of no queue growth on infra dashboards
- If gate fail: automatic rollback OR re-route to fallback model and notify oncall.

4) Rapid remediation recipes (first 10 minutes):
- If p95 latency rises and CPU/GPU utilization low -> increase batching window only for non-interactive routes, enable batching for background worker endpoints.
- If latency rises and GPU utilization high -> spin up additional nodes in dedicated pool (scale policy: +25% node count, cap at +100% during surge) and open surge rotation flow.
- If error rate spikes with stable infra -> toggle feature-flag to revert to previous model version, cut traffic by 50% to hosted fallback.
- If KV-cache miss rate high -> enable prefix-aggregation cache (short term), add warmup replay to build cache.

5) Monitoring dashboards & playbook links (quick list):
- Prodops Launch Board (Grafana): p50/p95/p99, error-rate, queue-depth, batch-size distribution.
- Model Serving Telemetry (Datadog): per-model latency heatmap, KV miss histogram.
- Cost burn (Billing console): real-time burn vs forecast in $/hour and $/1k tokens.
- Oncall Slack channel: #prodops-launch — include webhook for alerts.

6) Post-launch KPIs to watch (first 72h):
- Adoption/activation: daily active routes using new model, conversion delta vs control cohort.
- Quality regressions: prompt-eval drift flagged when BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim drop >3% on golden promptset.
- Long-tail errors: any novel error class appearing >10x baseline frequency.

7) Owner matrix (quick):
- Launch lead: Aisha Kapoor (product-ops) — decision authority for ramp pace.
- Serving runtime: Lucas Moretti — scale/rollback and kernel selection notes.
- SRE: Evelyn Chen — infra scale, autoscaler triggers, capacity adjustments.
- Solutions eng contact: Rashid Al-Fayeed — customer impact triage.

8) Risk heatmap (hand-wavy):
- High risk: sudden spike in long-tail latency due to large-sequence requests from a single customer — mitigations: per-customer throttles, request-size caps.
- Medium risk: KV-cache cold start from new prompt patterns — mitigations: warmup, lightweight caching layer.
- Low risk: cost overspend for bursty day — mitigations: budget throttle and routing to cheaper model variant.

9) Quick smoke tests (commands to run):
- curl -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate - payload sample (see snippet in Confluence)
- run replay: scripts/replay/traffic_replay --sample=1000 --rate=20/s --model=staging_v3
- verify metrics export: curl http://grafana.internal/api/datasource/prodops/query?p95

10) Open questions / next steps (notes-to-self):
- Need SLO definition alignment with legal for Dedicated SLA (Evelyn to confirm wording).
- Confirm cost-per-1k tokens for quantized models from infra benchmarking (Lucas).
- Add a short checklist for private deployments (VPC routing / KMS key rotation) — currently missing.

Appendix: short KPI table (paste into sheet later):
- KPI | Threshold | Measurement window | Owner
- p95 latency | <= 450ms | 15m rolling | Lucas
- Error rate | <= 0.3% | 5m rolling | Evelyn
- Cache hit ratio | >= 65% | 30m rolling | Rashid
- Cost per 1k tokens | within +/−10% forecast | 1h rolling | Product Finance

End.

Internal note: this doc intentionally mixes prescriptive thresholds and tactical remediations. The goal is to let launch leads convert fuzzy runway signals into a deterministic set of ops moves. Please comment inline rather than creating forks so we keep the checklist canonical.
